stem: Your team uses a Declarative Automation Bundle to deploy a job that queries a warehouse. The job must use a different warehouse id in dev, test, and prod, and the team must promote the same databricks.yml without editing it between deployments.

option_texts.A: Hard-code each warehouse id in the job resource and add a script that swaps them before deploy
option_texts.B: Keep one databricks.yml per environment and point the CI job at the matching file
option_texts.C: Declare a warehouse id as a custom variable and set its value per target, so one definition promotes unchanged
option_texts.D: Store the warehouse id in a secret scope and read it with spark.conf.set in every notebook

drill_answer_short: Declare a custom variable and set its value per target; the same configuration file then promotes across dev, test, and prod unchanged
decision_hinge: A custom variable is declared in the variables mapping, and you set its value when executing bundle commands, through an environment variable, elsewhere within your bundle configuration files, or in the .databricks/bundle/<target>/variable-overrides.json file.

plausible_options.B: must use a different warehouse id in dev, test, and prod

eliminated_by.A: the team must promote the same databricks.yml without editing it between deployments
eliminated_by.D: deploy a job that queries a warehouse

distractor_traps.A: T4: breaks a stated requirement - a swap script edits the deployed definition instead of promoting it unchanged
distractor_traps.B: T3: confusable sibling - per-environment files do vary the id, but they stop the team promoting one configuration
distractor_traps.D: T2: scope error - a secret scope hides a value at run time and does not parameterize a bundle resource

stem: You are working in a Databricks Git folder and must start feature work on a new branch before the job definition is deployed to production. Your team keeps all feature development on branches cut from main.

option_texts.A: Open the Lakeflow Jobs UI and add a job-scoped branch that applies to that job alone
option_texts.B: Run a bundle deploy with a branch flag so the CLI creates and checks out the branch
option_texts.C: Add a branch field to databricks.yml and reopen the workspace so the folder picks it up
option_texts.D: Open the Git dialog, click Create Branch, enter a name, select the base branch, and confirm

drill_answer_short: Branches are created from the Git dialog in the workspace UI: Create Branch, name it, pick the base branch
decision_hinge: To create a branch, click Create Branch, enter a name for the new branch and select the base branch, then click Create; to check out a different branch, use the branch dropdown in the Git dialog.

plausible_options.B: must start feature work on a new branch before the job definition is deployed to production

eliminated_by.A: Your team keeps all feature development on branches cut from main
eliminated_by.C: You are working in a Databricks Git folder

distractor_traps.A: T1: fabricated - there is no job-scoped branch in the Lakeflow Jobs UI
distractor_traps.B: T3: confusable sibling - the bundle CLI deploys resources and never manages Git branches for the folder
distractor_traps.C: T2: scope error - bundle configuration describes resources, not the Git state of the folder

stem: Your CI pipeline runs a bundle validate that passes, but the deploy then fails because a job references a value that is missing in the target workspace. The pipeline must supply that value at deploy time from the CI secret store, never from a file committed to the repo.

option_texts.A: Add a deploy hook that writes the value into the target workspace just before the deploy runs
option_texts.B: Declare it as a bundle variable and export BUNDLE_VAR_<name> with the value before the deploy runs
option_texts.C: Commit the value into databricks.yml in encrypted form and decrypt it during the deploy
option_texts.D: Change the job to read the value through spark.conf.get instead of the bundle configuration

drill_answer_short: Declare the value as a bundle variable and pass it in an environment variable named BUNDLE_VAR_<variable_name> at deploy time
decision_hinge: Provide the variable's value by setting an environment variable whose name must start with BUNDLE_VAR_, or provide the value as part of a bundle command such as validate or deploy.

plausible_options.A: must supply that value at deploy time from the CI secret store

eliminated_by.C: never from a file committed to the repo
eliminated_by.D: a job references a value that is missing in the target workspace

distractor_traps.A: T3: confusable sibling - a pre-deploy hook can seed a workspace, but the bundle still has no value bound to the variable
distractor_traps.C: T4: breaks a stated requirement - the value would live in a file committed to the repo
distractor_traps.D: T2: scope error - reading a Spark conf at run time does not resolve a missing bundle value at deploy time

stem: A bundle deploys a Lakeflow Declarative Pipeline plus a job that depends on it, to dev, test, and prod. The pipeline must read from a different source catalog in each of the three targets, and the team wants one pipeline resource defined only once.

option_texts.A: Define three pipeline resources, one per environment, and let the job pick the right one at run time
option_texts.B: Define the catalog in the metastore and have the pipeline look it up while it runs
option_texts.C: Define the dev catalog inline and hand-edit the bundle before each later deployment
option_texts.D: Define the pipeline once with its catalog set from a variable reference, then give that variable a value per target

drill_answer_short: One resource definition whose catalog comes from a variable reference, with the variable given a value per target
decision_hinge: You can reference a variable elsewhere within your bundle configuration files, and set its value per target in the .databricks/bundle/<target>/variable-overrides.json file.

plausible_options.A: must read from a different source catalog in each of the three targets

eliminated_by.B: A bundle deploys a Lakeflow Declarative Pipeline plus a job that depends on it
eliminated_by.C: the team wants one pipeline resource defined only once

distractor_traps.A: T3: confusable sibling - three resources do vary the catalog, but the pipeline is then defined three times
distractor_traps.B: T2: scope error - the metastore holds the catalog, not the deploy-time choice of which catalog this target reads
distractor_traps.C: T4: breaks a stated requirement - hand-editing between deployments is exactly what the team ruled out

stem: A CI stage must prove a Declarative Automation Bundle is syntactically correct and that its resource properties match the object schema. The stage must not create, change, or remove anything in the workspace.

option_texts.A: Run a bundle run so the resources execute once and surface any configuration errors
option_texts.B: Run a bundle deploy with a dry run flag to preview the changes it would apply
option_texts.C: Run a bundle validate, which checks the configuration files and reports schema warnings
option_texts.D: Run a bundle sync so the files reach the workspace and the schema is checked there

drill_answer_short: bundle validate checks that configuration files are syntactically correct and warns on properties missing from the object schema
decision_hinge: The bundle validate command validates that bundle configuration files are syntactically correct and outputs warnings if resource properties are defined in the bundle configuration files that are not found in the corresponding object's schema.

plausible_options.B: must prove a Declarative Automation Bundle is syntactically correct

eliminated_by.A: The stage must not create, change, or remove anything in the workspace
eliminated_by.D: its resource properties match the object schema

distractor_traps.A: T4: breaks a stated requirement - running the resources changes workspace state
distractor_traps.B: T3: confusable sibling - a deploy preview also reports problems, but it belongs to the deploy path rather than a check
distractor_traps.D: T2: scope error - syncing files moves content to the workspace instead of checking the configuration
